significant deviations in scope [service=recommendationservice]: recommendationservice_latency-50 z=773.71 (44400.8%); recommendationservice_latency-90 z=700.32 (80358.5%); recommendationservice_socket z=86.98 (434.9%); recommendationservice_mem z=41.08 (205.4%)

alternatives_rejected.why: Their error z-scores in E1 come with no own-latency deviation and are consistent with errors propagating from downstream calls to recommendationservice (E2 inbound errors 0.0->0.51). Note E5's worst traces are frontend->checkout paths, which is not direct proof.
E5 shows a few error traces through checkout, but the all-service metric ranking in E1 shows no checkoutservice deviation. Only recommendationservice shows both metric and trace anomalies (E2, E3).
Injected delay would raise caller-observed latency sharply. E2 shows inbound self-time p50 rising only 1.11x, while inbound errors jump to 0.51, which fits dropped packets better than a pure delay.

The socket metric rise (E3 z=86.98) is lower-ranked than the latency deviation and can come from retransmits or connections left hanging under loss. Socket exhaustion would also tend to surface as the service's own errors, which stay at 0.0 (E2).
The mem deviation (E3 z=41.08) is the weakest signal. Memory pressure would not explain errors seen only by callers while the service's own spans stay error-free (E2).

proposed_fix.description: Inspect the recommendationservice pod's network path (e.g. tc/netem qdisc, CNI/sidecar drops) and remove the packet-loss rule or reschedule the pod onto a healthy node. Then confirm inbound error rate and latency-50/90 return to baseline.
